subject: Order Form: pricing phasing, minimum commit phasing, invoice routing & tax evidence
messages:
From: James Lee <james.lee@medsprint.com>

Cc: Paige Tran <paige.tran@medsprint.com>, ProcureOps <procureops@medsprint.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order form queries: invoice routing + tax evidence

Camila — thanks for sending the draft Order Form and the MSA redlines. A couple of items the procurement team asked me to confirm before we proceed to legal: 

1) Invoice routing: our accounting team requires invoices sent to billing@medsprint.com and a separate PO reference on each invoice. Can Redwood route invoices to a different legal entity if needed? We also need confirmation on whether invoices can be split across entities for the phased minimum commit.

2) Minimum commit phasing: the draft shows a single annual commit. We need a 3-tranche schedule (Q3, Q1 next fiscal year, Q3 next fiscal year) with associated invoice dates. Can you propose an invoice calendar we can review?

3) Tax/residency evidence: procurement asks for Redwood's VAT/Tax residency certificate to support withholding tax treatment in some countries. Can you attach what you have and confirm whether we need a W-8/W-9 or country-specific docs?

If you can share exemplar invoice lines and a proposed payment calendar that maps to the commit tranches, that'll speed things up on our side.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if useful.

—James
James Lee
Head of Procurement, Medsprint

Hi James — thanks for the clear list. See answers below and attached drafts. Quick summary up front: yes to split invoicing across entities (with accounting caveats), we propose the 3-tranche invoice calendar attached, and we've included our standard tax residency statement and an FAQ on W-8/W-9. 

Attachments: MSA_Redline_20250623.pdf (redlines), OrderForm_ProposedPaymentSchedule.xlsx (3-tranche calendar), TaxResidencyCertificate.pdf (company tax doc), plus a short invoice template.

Details:
- Invoice routing: Redwood can send invoices from the entity that signs the Order Form. If you need invoices split across Medsprint entities, we can accommodate but we need the PO numbers and invoice-to entities on the Order Form. Our accounting team requires a single payment remittance entity per invoice. 

- Minimum commit phasing: attached spreadsheet has suggested invoice dates and amounts for the 3 tranches you mentioned. Each tranche will generate a separate invoice; net terms in the draft are Net 45 from invoice date. If you'd like Net 30/Net 60 options we can mark those in the spreadsheet.

- Tax evidence: attached tax residency certificate. For US customers we usually provide W-9; for non-US withholding we provide tax residency as needed. If Medsprint requires notarized or apostilled copies, let me know — we can escalate to finance.

Next steps: I want to loop in our finance and legal to confirm the wording for split-entity invoicing and to make sure the payment calendar aligns with Redwood's revenue recognition (we've seen edge cases when invoices are split across legal entities). Can I introduce Kimberly (Finance) and Karthik (Legal) on this thread?

If yes, I'll tee up a short redline call for tomorrow.

Best,

Kimberly, Karthik — forwarding Medsprint's ask. Key items they need:
- Confirmation we can issue invoices split across two Medsprint entities (they want a tranche tied to Entity A and a tranche tied to Entity B). Our current Order Form ties invoices to the signing entity.
- Net terms: they prefer Net 45 but asked if Net 30/60 alternatives available. Any revenue recognition or collection concerns?
- Tax residency / withholding: they requested Redwood's tax residency document; I've attached the certificate. If Procurement requires a specific clause around withholding gross-up or responsibility, please propose language.

Attachments forwarded: MSA_Redline_20250623.pdf; OrderForm_ProposedPaymentSchedule.xlsx; TaxResidencyCertificate.pdf

Thanks — Camila
From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: camila_reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Jun 2025 10:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Order form queries: invoice routing + tax evidence — please advise on redlines

Camila — quick notes after an initial pass. I also attached an annotated OrderForm PDF (inline comments). High level:

1) Split-entity invoicing: acceptable operationally but must be explicitly captured in the Order Form. Proposed clause: "Invoices will be issued by the Redwood entity identified on each invoice and payment will be routed to the remittance address specified. Customer may designate different invoice-to legal entities per tranche by providing PO numbers and entity legal name at least 14 days prior to invoice date." This covers our AR expectations.

2) Net terms: stick with Net 45 as the default. If Medsprint requests Net 30 on a tranche-by-tranche basis we can accommodate but we need pre-approval for cash application changes and that may delay recognition. If they push for Net 30 across the board, CFO sign-off required.

3) Withholding & tax: do not accept gross-up obligations. Proposed language: Customer is responsible for any withholding taxes imposed by its jurisdiction; Customer will provide tax-deductible certificates where required and will notify Redwood within 30 days of any withholding assessment. We will provide standard tax residency docs (attached). If they demand additional indemnity, escalate to VP Finance.

4) Invoice lines & PO: require that PO number be on the invoice and that the invoice line references the tranche (e.g., "FY26 Tranche 1 - Minimum Commit").

5) Attachments: I've included suggested redline for the billing table and payment schedule. See attachment: OrderForm_AnnotatedForMedsprint.pdf (embedded comments).

If Karthik can confirm legal wording on the split-entity clause and withholding language I will prepare the final redline. I can also propose a payment calendar that maps exactly to the 3 tranches with invoice dates: 2025-08-01, 2026-01-15, 2026-08-01.

—Kimberly

Hi James — looping back with an agreed approach after finance/legal review. TL;DR: we can do split-entity invoicing per tranche, default Net 45, and we provide tax residency docs (no gross-up). Please find the attached final redline and a proposed invoice calendar.

What changed since my last note:
- Added explicit split-entity invoicing clause (see Section 2.1 in redline). We require PO numbers and legal entity names 14 days prior to invoice date.
- Net terms remain Net 45. If you need Net 30 for a specific tranche, indicate it in the PO and we'll escalate to CFO.
- Withholding: Customer responsible for withholding taxes. Redwood will provide tax residency documentation; Redwood won't accept gross-up.
- Invoice labeling: each invoice will include "Tranche X - Minimum Commit" in the description and reference the PO.

Attachments: MSA_Redline_20250623.pdf, OrderForm_ProposedPaymentSchedule.xlsx, TaxResidencyCertificate.pdf. Also a DocuSign packet has been prepared pending your confirmation of invoice-to entity names and PO numbers. DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/redirect?env=prod&acct=00A1&doc=0f9a

1) Confirm the invoice-to legal entity names and PO numbers for each tranche by EOD Mon 30 Jun.
2) If any tranche needs Net 30, flag which one and provide contact for CFO approval.
3) Reply-all to confirm and we'll send the DocuSign envelope.

If you'd prefer a 20-minute call to run through the calendar, I'm available Mon afternoon PT.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.
